sections.title: Read the passage and fill in the blanks.

questions.q: Under the British Raj, Indian art displayed a general ______.
Miniatures were ousted by European ______ painting.
______ of Kerala was famous for mythological subjects and portraiture.
______ tried to recreate a new style in painting.
The ______ School emerged in the first half of the 20th century.

sections.passage: At the beginning of the 19th century under the influence of the British Raj, Indian art displayed a general decline. The craft and techniques of fresco and miniature paintings were nearly lost. Miniatures were ousted by European oil painting. Raja Ravi Varma of Kerala was famous for his paintings of mythological subjects and portraiture. His works showed western influence in his oil paintings. On the other hand, Abanindranath Tagore tried to recreate a new style in painting. Nandalal Bose, Benode Behari and a few others followed this newly awakened sense of nationalism. Thus emerged the Bengal School in the first half of the 20th century. (April 2026)

sections.passage: Raja Ravi Varma is one of the most celebrated painters of India. His life began in a small village of Kilimanoor, Kerala. He was a prominent representative of the Europeanised school of Indian artists. He gained reputation for his water and oil colour techniques. A vast panorama of India's mythology is portrayed in series of his works that mostly project the heroines as central figures. His works are still visible in prints, calendars, posters and oleographs. Hamsa Damayanti was painted in 1899 in oil and it created a sensation when first displayed at the Madras Fine Arts Exhibition. (October 2025)

sections.title: Read the passage and state whether each statement is true or false.

questions.q: The Company School produced significant works in the British period.
Raja Ravi Varma did not follow the western style.
questions.answer: False – he followed the western style while reviving Indian subjects.

questions.q: The Bengal School was established in Santiniketan.
Amrita Shergil followed a particular Indian school.
questions.answer: False – she did not follow any Indian school.

sections.passage: Modern Indian art is very much related to the history of the country and social conditions in which the artists developed their styles. We see the growth of different schools after the decline of British Raj. The British period produced significant works under the Company School. The Indian artists followed the European techniques in their paintings. Raja Ravi Varma served as a bridge to revive Indian subjects but followed western style. Later the Bengal School established in Santiniketan served as a centre of artistic development. Abanindranath Tagore and his disciples contributed on a large scale. The best and most individualistic painter was probably Amrita Shergil. She did not follow any Indian school. (April 2024)

questions.q: Gaganendranath Tagore was born in Kolkata.
He painted sketches of the Himalayas between 1910 and 1921.
He blindly imitated western art.
questions.answer: False – he never blindly imitated the West.

questions.q: 'The Atrium' shows Surrealist influence.

sections.passage: Gaganendranath Tagore was born in 1867 in Kolkata. His important works from 1910 to 1921 were the sketches of the Himalayas, the life of Chaitanya and drawings depicting Indian life. He supported his brother Abanindranath but also showed an inclination towards the Cubist school in Europe. He never blindly imitated western art. His social cartoons were very popular and reflected the funny side of the life of the citizens of Kolkata. He is best known for political cartoons and social satires on Westernised Bengalis. 'The Atrium' is a fine example of Cubist influence on his work.

questions.q: Write in brief about Amrita Shergil.
questions.answer: Amrita Shergil (born 1913) had a Sikh father and a Hungarian mother, studied art in Paris and was influenced by the Post-Impressionists, Modigliani and Gauguin. After coming to India in 1921 she drew inspiration from Kangra miniatures and Ajanta frescoes. Her works include 'The Bride's Toilette' and 'Brahmacharies'. She is the first lady of modern Indian art and painted only for seven years.

questions.q: Write in brief about Raja Ravi Varma.
questions.answer: Raja Ravi Varma (born at Kilimanoor, Kerala) was a prominent representative of the Europeanised school, famous for oil and water colour portraits and mythological paintings (Hamsa Damayanti, Dushyanta–Shakuntala) with heroines as central figures. His oleographs spread in prints and calendars; he linked traditional Indian art with Western realism.

questions.q: Write in brief what kind of art evolved after Company Art declined in India.
questions.answer: After Company Art declined, Indian artists turned to their own heritage and the Bengal School emerged at Santiniketan under Abanindranath Tagore, Nandalal Bose and others, using Indian classics and mythology with idealism, rejecting western realism; Jamini Roy, Rabindranath Tagore, Gaganendranath Tagore and Amrita Shergil followed.

questions.q: Describe the painting 'The Atrium'.
questions.answer: 'The Atrium' (water colour on paper, 1920, 12.5 x 9.5 in) by Gaganendranath Tagore is a fine example of Cubist influence. It combines geometrical shapes in various shades and tints with a dramatic play of light and abstraction in the shapes.

questions.q: Which European styles influenced Amrita Shergil most?
questions.answer: Post-Impressionism – the Post-Impressionists such as Modigliani and Gauguin.

questions.q: What does the painting 'Hamsa Damayanti' depict?
questions.answer: It shows Damayanti in a red sari lovingly listening to the messages of her lover Nala narrated by a swan (hamsa); her silent love is shown in the sparkle of her eyes and the glow of her cheeks.

questions.q: Name two characteristics of the composition of 'Brahmacharies'.
questions.answer: It is composed on a horizontal plane with vertical placement of the five figures; a deep red background, white dhotis and a neutral greenish-grey foreground give a calm composition.

questions.q: What was the contribution of the Bengal School?
questions.answer: It revived Indian painting after Company Art by taking inspiration from Indian classics, miniatures, frescoes and folk art and gave a starting point to the movement of contemporary Indian art.

sections.title: Short answer question. Answer in 50–60 words.

questions.q: Describe the subjects and technique of Raja Ravi Varma's paintings.
questions.answer: He painted mythological subjects and portraits – episodes from Dushyanta–Shakuntala, Nala–Damayanti and the Mahabharata, with heroines as central figures, and Indian divinities. His technique was Western academic realism in oil and water colour, and his oleographs spread his pictures as prints, calendars and posters.

questions.q: Describe the composition of 'Brahmacharies' by Amrita Shergil.
questions.answer: Painted in 1938, it shows five young Brahmin students in an ashram as symbols of devotion. The composition is on a horizontal plane with vertical placement of figures; the deep red background, subtle white dhotis and greenish-grey foreground keep it calm, and the off-white central figure with black and brown bodies stands out.

sections.title: Long answer question. Answer in 70–80 words.

questions.q: Write an appreciative essay on Gaganendranath Tagore.
questions.answer: Gaganendranath Tagore (born 1867 in Kolkata, died 1938) was a leading figure of contemporary Indian painting. In 1910–21 he made sketches of the Himalayas, a sequence on the life of Chaitanya and drawings of Indian life. He supported his brother Abanindranath but inclined towards European Cubism and, after long experiment, developed his own brand: overlapping flattened geometrical shapes of colour create a mysterious world with a dramatic play of light and shade; he never blindly imitated the West. 'The Atrium' (1920, water colour on paper) is a fine example, composed of various shades and tints of geometrical shapes. He was also a great critic whose cartoons and satires on Westernised Bengalis were popular.

questions.q: Review the evolution of Modern Indian Art.
questions.answer: Under British rule Indian art declined; miniatures and fresco were nearly lost and European oil painting and the Company School replaced them. Raja Ravi Varma bridged Indian subjects and western style. Abanindranath Tagore, Nandalal Bose and Benode Behari started the Bengal School at Santiniketan, taking subjects from Indian classics and mythology and rejecting western realism; Jamini Roy modernised folk art; Rabindranath Tagore added expression; Gaganendranath Tagore used cubist forms; Amrita Shergil blended Western training and Indian tradition. The Bengal School gave the starting point for contemporary Indian art.

questions.q: Which European styles influenced Amrita Shergil most? What are the characteristics of the 'Brahmacharies' painting?
questions.answer: She studied in Paris and was influenced by Post-Impressionists like Modigliani and Gauguin, and she drew on Kangra miniatures and Ajanta frescoes. 'Brahmacharies' (1938, oil on canvas, National Gallery of Modern Art, New Delhi) shows five young Brahmin students as symbols of devotion, on a horizontal plane with vertical figures, a deep red background, subtle whites of dhotis and a neutral greenish-grey foreground giving calm.
